description: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across 23 layers, using a threshold of 1e-3, under three conditions: before gating, after gating, and after average gating. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 23 with integer tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.8 in linear scale, with tick marks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. The blue dashed line, representing “sparsity ratio before gate,” remains near zero across all layers, with an average of 0.003. The orange dotted line, “sparsity ratio after gate,” starts near 0.85 at layer 0, drops sharply to around 0.4 by layer 2, continues decreasing to ~0.1 by layer 8, and stabilizes near 0.02–0.05 from layer 10 onward, with an overall average of 0.126. The green dash-dot line, “sparsity ratio after average gate,” begins at ~0.8 at layer 0, declines steeply to ~0.25 by layer 3, then gradually decreases to ~0.05 by layer 10, and remains near 0.02–0.03 for the remaining layers, with an average of 0.080. All three lines show a general decline in sparsity ratio with increasing layer number, with the gated conditions exhibiting significantly higher sparsity than the pre-gate condition.
